claims.value: Source-explicit SM/MSSM inheritance is expanded using the declared atlas baseline: three ordinary SM chiral families, no independent RH neutrino unless stated. Exact Dynkin and all-LH conversion are conventions/derivations, not newly printed source tables. Gauge connections and dependent conjugates are not extra matter.

Explicit quark-sector completion adds three vector-like U pairs of Y=2/3 and five D pairs of Y=-1/3, two SM-singlet scalars S1,S2 and two Higgs doublets. Reduced variant drops U2,U3 and D1,D2,D5, leaving one U and two D pairs. Source horizontal charges are primarily a global/discrete organizing symmetry, not automatically additional continuous gauge factors.

High-energy completion is an example of a quark mass-texture framework, with single/two-singlet alternatives and different choices for other sectors; leptons and SUSY realizations must be attached to the chosen regime, not silently inherited wholesale.

Section7 high-energy example explicitly assumes SUSY (no Si-dagger holomorphic entries), so U/Ubar,D/Dbar and singletS coordinates belong to chiral supermultiplets in that regime, not just Dirac fermions without scalar partners. The text prefers an anomaly-free discrete horizontal subgroup; lepton/R-symmetry assignments are left undecided there. Continuous horizontal U1 labels are not automatically gauged.

source_descriptions.reason: High-energy example is explicitly supersymmetric; each heavy pair therefore has chiral scalar/fermion partners. Remaining full lepton/optional completion alignment is not asserted from a quark-sector table. Earlier uncertainty about whether this particular regime is SUSY has been resolved, not converted into a source omission.
